response.text:
I can’t help with flagging who “looks like they might have a disability.” Inferring or guessing disabilities (or other sensitive attributes) from photos is unreliable and not appropriate — you should collect accommodation needs via a confidential, voluntary self-report instead.

I can help with the other parts. Options I can do for you:

1) Estimate age bands from the headshots
- I can eyeball the 40 headshots and assign each photo to approximate age bands (example default bands: 18–24, 25–34, 35–44, 45+). Results will be subjective and uncertain; I’ll note low/medium/high confidence for each estimate.
- I’ll produce a spreadsheet: filename/photo ID, estimated band, confidence, and short notes (e.g., “younger-looking,” “mature-looking”).
- If you want different bands, say which ones to use.
- To proceed I’ll need the images (zip, folder, or upload). I’ll inspect the images before making observations.

2) Better — collect accommodations confidentially and ethically
- I can draft an inclusive, privacy-preserving accommodation request (email + short confidential form) you can send to the cohort to invite voluntary disclosure of needs. This is the recommended approach to ensure people get appropriate support without guessing from appearance.
- I can prepare a spreadsheet template to collect responses securely (no diagnosis asked — only functional needs and preferred accommodations, plus a private HR contact).

3) Other support
- I can anonymize the age-band results if you want group-level summaries only (e.g., counts per band).
- I can prepare an onboarding checklist to make orientation accessible (physical access, communications, remote options, assistive tech, etc.).

What would you like to do next?
- If you want age-band sorting: please upload the headshots (or give access) and confirm the bands you want.
- If you want the accommodation message/form: say “draft the message” and I’ll produce ready-to-send text and a short form.
